title: Behavioral bounds and migration hatches for pinned-model stability
creator: Rina Patel
description: Define a pragmatic, machine-readable contract for pinned model versions that specifies behavioral bounds (semantic deltas, output-shape tolerances, and parameter aliasing rules) and a set of approved migration hatches (adaptive parameter mapping, transparent fallback selection, and conversion shims). This ticket captures the spec, acceptance criteria, telemetry gates, and a short-term implementation plan for runtime enforcement and onboarding checks. The goal is to let customers pin versions with clear expectations about what may change, what is forbidden, and what automated mitigation the platform will apply when small deltas are detected.
background: We need a repeatable contract that balances developer expectations (no surprising output regressions for pinned versions) with operational practicality (minor tokenizer/formatting normalization and harmless parameter aliases). Existing documents focus on IO fingerprints and strict contracts; this spec introduces explicit tolerance bands and 'migration hatches'—well-scoped automated fixes that the runtime may apply without breaking the pin guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable spec (YAML/JSON schema) describing: allowed output-shape variance, tokenization-normalization rules, parameter alias mapping table, and maximum semantic-distance thresholds
Runtime enforcer that rejects model onboarding if spec is missing or if measured deltas exceed thresholds
Telemetry dashboard showing per-pin semantic distance, output-shape violations, and number of automatic hatch activations
A documented migration-hatch catalog with exact transforms, fallback model selection policy, and admin override flow
Onboarding checklist and sample conformance tests that members of model-onboarding can run locally and in CI
proposed_approach: Schema: define 'behavioral_bound' fields: max_token_diff_percent, max_structural_diff_examples, semantic_distance_threshold (embedding cosine) and parameter_alias_map
Validation: run anchor prompt suite against candidate model and baseline pinned artifact to compute metrics; fail onboarding if metrics exceed thresholds
Hatches: provide small transformations (normalize whitespace/tokenization, canonicalize date/time formats, map deprecated param names) applied at the routing layer with explicit audit trail
Fallbacks: when semantic_distance is high but within safety band, route to fallback model variant with a compatibility shim and surface warnings in console
Rollout: start as 'opt-in advisor' during Cycle 41, then gate enforcement behind project flags and runtime-1.22 release
tradeoffs_and_risks: Strict enforcement reduces customer surprise but increases onboarding friction and churn for model vendors
Lenient tolerances allow silent regressions—must be mitigated by strong telemetry and quick rollback/alerting
Automatic shims reduce customer work but may mask real regressions; all shims must be reversible and logged
Semantic-distance metrics depend on prompt suite quality; incomplete suites can produce false negatives/positives

decisions: Use embedding cosine distance (instruction-tuned small eval suite) as primary semantic metric
Allow parameter aliasing table for obvious name mappings (e.g., 'max_tokens' -> 'max_new_tokens') but reject semantic parameter re-interpretations
Hatches are opt-in during initial rollout and require explicit audit log entries when used
Do not attempt automated model patching beyond deterministic text transforms in the first release
